questions.q: For the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane and anhydrous AlCl3, which statements are correct? A. Major product is n-propylbenzene. B. Isopropyl carbocation intermediate is also generated. C. Multiple substitution is inevitable. D. Introducing an electron-donating substituent on benzene will not produce any alkylbenzene.
questions.explain: The 1° carbocation rearranges to isopropyl, so the major product is isopropylbenzene; the alkyl product is more reactive, so polysubstitution happens.

questions.q: Identify the correct statements. The presence of a -NO2 group in a benzene ring: A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions. D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
questions.explain: NO2 withdraws by -M and -I: deactivates EAS, makes nucleophilic substitution easier.

questions.q: Benzene on nitration gives nitrobenzene in the presence of HNO3 and H2SO4 mixture, where:
options: both H2SO4 and HNO3 act as bases
HNO3 acts as an acid and H2SO4 acts as a base
both H2SO4 and HNO3 act as acids
HNO3 acts as a base and H2SO4 acts as an acid
questions.explain: H2SO4 protonates HNO3, which loses water to form NO2+; the proton acceptor (HNO3) is the base here.

questions.q: The correct sequence of reagents used in the preparation of 4-bromo-2-nitroethylbenzene from benzene is:
questions.explain: Acylate first (no rearrangement), Clemmensen-reduce to ethyl (o/p director), brominate para, then nitration goes ortho to ethyl.

questions.q: Polysubstitution is a major drawback in:
questions.explain: The alkyl product is more reactive than benzene, so it keeps reacting; acylation products are deactivated, so it stops at one.

questions.q: The increasing order of reactivity of the following compounds towards aromatic electrophilic substitution reaction is: A = chlorobenzene, B = anisole, C = toluene, D = benzonitrile
questions.explain: Benzonitrile is most deactivated (-M), chlorobenzene deactivating but o/p, toluene activates mildly, anisole activates strongly.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of reagents used for converting nitrobenzene into m-dibromobenzene?
questions.explain: NO2 is meta-directing, so brominate first; then reduce to aniline, diazotise, and Sandmeyer replaces N2+ with Br at that same position.
